title: 2 Chronicles 22:10–12
context: After Ahaziah’s death, his mother Athaliah sets out to destroy the royal family of Judah and seize power. Jehoshabeath, Ahaziah’s sister and the wife of Jehoiada the priest, rescues the infant Joash and hides him in God’s house for six years. The parallel is 2 Kings 11:1–3. Both traditions read the passage with sorrow at Athaliah’s violence and honor Jehoshabeath’s courage, seeing in the hidden child God’s faithfulness to his promise to David, as in the notes on 2 Samuel 7 and 1 Chronicles 17.

verses.text: Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring of the house of Judah.
verses.arminianNotes:
When Athaliah sees that her son is dead, she sets out to destroy all the royal offspring of the house of Judah. The narrator records this in one sober sentence.

Arminian readers see a deliberate and grievous choice driven by ambition, for which Athaliah is fully responsible.
verses.reformedNotes:
The verse closely follows 2 Kings 11:1, adding ‘of the house of Judah.’ Her act threatened the line through which God had promised a lamp to David (21:7).

Reformed readers see God’s promise seemingly near extinction. Both traditions read this with sorrow as shared ground.

verses.text: But Jehoshabeath, the king’s daughter, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stealthily rescued him from among the king’s sons who were slain, and put him and his nurse in the bedroom. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of King Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest (for she was the sister of Ahaziah), hid him from Athaliah, so that she didn’t kill him.
verses.arminianNotes:
Jehoshabeath, King Jehoram’s daughter and Ahaziah’s sister, rescues the infant Joash from among the king’s sons being killed and hides him with his nurse. Chronicles adds that she was the wife of Jehoiada the priest.

Arminian readers honor her free and courageous act.
verses.reformedNotes:
2 Kings 11:2 calls her Jehosheba and does not mention her marriage. Her marriage links the rescue with the priestly household that follows.

Reformed readers see God preserving David’s line through one woman’s courage. Both traditions honor Jehoshabeath as shared ground.

verses.text: He was with them hidden in God’s house six years while Athaliah reigned over the land.
verses.arminianNotes:
Joash remains hidden with them in God’s house for six years while Athaliah reigns over the land. The rightful heir grows up in hiding.

Arminian readers see sustained faithfulness from those who protected the child over many years.
verses.reformedNotes:
Where 2 Kings 11:3 says he was hidden with her in the LORD’s house, Chronicles says with them in God’s house, perhaps including Jehoiada.

Reformed readers see God sheltering David’s heir in his own house. Both traditions read this as shared ground, consistent with the 2 Kings 11 notes.
